'''Sandro Stringari''' is an Italian theoretical physicist who has contributed to the theory of quantum many-body physics, including atomic nuclei, [[quantum liquid]]s and ultra-cold atomic [[Bose gas|Bose]] and [[Fermi gas]]es. He has developed in a systematic way the sum rule approach to the collective behavior of interacting systems.

==Biography==
After the studies at the University of Pisa and at the Scuola Normale Superiore Pisa, completed in 1972 and supervised by [[Bruno Touschek]], he moved to Trento and Oxford under the supervision of Renzo Leonardi and [[:de:David M. Brink|David Brink]], respectively. In the years 1978/79 and 1985/86, invited by [[Oriol Bohigas Marti]], he has worked at the Institut de Physique Nucleaire in Orsay. In 1990, he became full professor at the University of Trento, where he currently teaches an undergraduate course on quantum mechanics and a graduate course on quantum gases and superfluidity.<ref>{{cite web |title=UniTrento - Sandro Stringari - Teaching |url=https://webapps.unitn.it/du/en/Persona/PER0003537/Didattica |access-date=24 February 2019}}</ref> In 2002, he established in Trento the Center on Bose –Einstein Condensation, founded by the Istituto Nazionale per la Fisica della Materia (INFM), and now part of CNR. In the year 2004/2005, invited by [[Claude Cohen-Tannoudji]], he held the European Chair at the [[Collège de France]], in Paris. In 2010, he was recipient of the 5 years [[European Research Council#Advanced Grants|ERC Advanced Grant]] "Quantum Gases beyond equilibrium". Since 2011, he is corresponding member of the [[Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]].

==Main scientific contributions==
In the first period of his scientific career Sandro Stringari focused on the magnetic properties of atomic nuclei and on the isospin degree of freedom, developing the innovative '''sum rule approach''' to the collective excitations.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lipparini | first1=E. | last2=Stringari | first2=S. | title=Sum rules and giant resonances in nuclei | journal=Physics Reports | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=175 | issue=3–4 | year=1989 | issn=0370-1573 | doi=10.1016/0370-1573(89)90029-x | pages=103–261| bibcode=1989PhR...175..103L }}</ref>

Starting from the 80’s he oriented his interests in the direction of '''atomic clusters''' and '''quantum liquids'''. Major contributions of this period are the study of the evaporation mechanism of helium clusters <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Brink | first1=D. M. | last2=Stringari | first2=S. | title=Density of states and evaporation rate of helium clusters | journal=Zeitschrift für Physik D | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=15 | issue=3 | year=1990 | issn=0178-7683 | doi=10.1007/bf01437187 | pages=257–263| bibcode=1990ZPhyD..15..257B | s2cid=84178148 }}</ref> and the '''T=0 extension of the Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner theorem'''.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Pitaevskii | first1=L. | last2=Stringari | first2=S. | title=Uncertainty principle, quantum fluctuations, and broken symmetries | journal=Journal of Low Temperature Physics | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=85 | issue=5–6 | year=1991 | issn=0022-2291 | doi=10.1007/bf00682193 | pages=377–388| bibcode=1991JLTP...85..377P | s2cid=121848601 }}</ref>

His interests in the physics of '''Bose-Einstein condensates''' (BEC) started with the workshop on Bose-Einstein Condensation (BEC), known as the "Levico conference", organized in 1993 at Levico.<ref>Bose Einstein Condensation Proceedings of the 1993  Levico International Workshop, A. Griffin, D. Snoke and S. Stringari eds. (Cambridge University Press, 1995)</ref> After the first experimental realization of BEC in 1995, he developed the formalism of superfluid hydrodynamics to describe the '''collective oscillations''' of a harmonically trapped BECs, providing analytic predictions for their frequencies.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Stringari | first=S. | title=Collective Excitations of a Trapped Bose-Condensed Gas | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=77 | issue=12 | date=1996-09-16 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.77.2360 | pages=2360–2363| pmid=10061934 |arxiv=cond-mat/9603126| bibcode=1996PhRvL..77.2360S | s2cid=981505 }}</ref> This contribution had a major impact on the first generation of experiments on ultra cold quantum gases and influenced an important line of theoretical work. Later contributions to the dynamics of trapped quantum gases, and to '''their rotational, superfluid and thermodynamic properties''' are summarized in the review papers on Bose-Einstein condensates <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Dalfovo | first1=Franco | last2=Giorgini | first2=Stefano | last3=Pitaevskii | first3=Lev P. | last4=Stringari | first4=Sandro | title=Theory of Bose-Einstein condensation in trapped gases | journal=Reviews of Modern Physics | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=71 | issue=3 | date=1999-04-01 | issn=0034-6861 | doi=10.1103/revmodphys.71.463 | pages=463–512|arxiv=cond-mat/9806038| bibcode=1999RvMP...71..463D | s2cid=55787701 }}</ref> and Fermi gases <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Giorgini | first1=Stefano | last2=Pitaevskii | first2=Lev P. | last3=Stringari | first3=Sandro | title=Theory of ultracold atomic Fermi gases | journal=Reviews of Modern Physics | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=80 | issue=4 | date=2008-10-02 | issn=0034-6861 | doi=10.1103/revmodphys.80.1215 | pages=1215–1274|arxiv=0706.3360| bibcode=2008RvMP...80.1215G | s2cid=117755089 }}</ref> as well as in the book on Bose-Einstein Condensation and Superfluidity <ref>Bose-Einstein Condensation and Superfluidity<br />[[Lev Pitaevskii]] and Sandro Stringari,  Int. Series of Monographs on Physics ({{cite book |title=Bose-Einstein Condensation and Superfluidity |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2016 |isbn=9780198758884|pages=576|issue=164 }})</ref> written in collaboration with [[Lev Pitaevskii]].
